articles.title: 'Window for military action narrowing': Trump urged to launch new campaign against Iran before January
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump's advisers have urged him to launch fresh military strikes against Iran before a new Democratic-controlled Congress takes office
articles.body: US President Donald Trump's advisers have urged him to launch fresh military strikes against Iran before a new Democratic-controlled Congress takes office in January, warning that the window for military action could narrow once lawmakers return to Washington, according to a report by NBC News.Citing two US officials, NBC News reported that administration and defence officials had told Trump that a new Congress could complicate any military campaign through investigations, restrictions on funding or resolutions seeking to block further strikes. Some advisers have therefore pushed for renewed military action before January, although the president has yet to make a decision.Trump received an updated briefing on Thursday on the Iranian threat and the military options available to Washington. The meeting was attended by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman General Dan Caine. According to the report, Hegseth has continued to advocate renewed strikes, while other members of the administration have cautioned that further escalation could derail diplomatic efforts.Vice President JD Vance, meanwhile, has been pursuing negotiations with Tehran in an attempt to prevent another round of conflict. A fresh military campaign, if authorised, could be shorter but more intense than previous operations, with Iran's oil and gas infrastructure and nuclear facilities, including the Pickaxe Mountain site, among the potential targets discussed with Trump.A White House official told NBC News that Trump had "all options available at any time", adding that only the president knew what he would do and when.The push for a military decision comes amid parallel diplomatic efforts to prevent tensions from escalating further. Qatar has been mediating between Washington and Tehran, with two Middle East government officials telling the Associated Press that Iran was reviewing proposals from Doha aimed at resolving differences over its nuclear programme.Trump also spoke to Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani on Friday about efforts to de-escalate tensions and secure a comprehensive agreement. The Qatari leader emphasised dialogue and diplomatic solutions, warning against further escalation and stressing the importance of protecting maritime navigation and energy supplies.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has also held telephone conversations with regional counterparts, including officials from Iraq and Tunisia, to discuss diplomatic efforts. Tehran's proposed framework reportedly includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, setting a timetable for negotiations and addressing its nuclear programme.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'A soulful rendition’: Rajnath Singh shares video of IAF warriors' patriotic melody
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday shared a video of Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel singing a patriotic song, praising their musical
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday shared a video of Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel singing a patriotic song, praising their musical talent and saying their performance reflected the passion and dedication with which they serve the country.In the clip, which is shared on X, showed two uniformed IAF air warriors singing together in a large hall.The personnel sang lines including "Jeene ki ijazat de de ya hukm shahadat de de" and "O des mere" in the 45-second video.Sharing the video, Rajnath Singh described the performance as a "soulful rendition" and praised the air warriors for bringing the same commitment to music that they demonstrate in their service."A soulful rendition by our talented IAF Air Warriors! Their voices reflect the same passion, pride and dedication that define their service to the nation. Truly a treat to listen to!" he wrote on X.Earlier, Rajnath Singh urged the armed forces to remain on the highest alert to deal with emerging threats to India's national security, warning that adversaries could use misinformation and social media to target both soldiers and local residents.Addressing air warriors at the Bagdogra Air Force Station in West Bengal, near the frontier with China in the eastern sector, Singh said the nature of security threats was changing and that the military needed to prepare for challenges beyond conventional warfare.Without naming any country, he said adversaries were increasingly looking to exploit weaknesses rather than engage in direct military confrontation."Often, the adversary avoids direct confrontation and instead seeks to exploit our vulnerabilities. Through social media, the adversary may attempt to sow doubt in the minds of the local population and our soldiers by spreading misleading information," he said."In such a scenario, your role extends beyond that of an ordinary soldier," he added.According to the Defence Ministry, Singh called for the armed forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, with particular attention to domain awareness, cyber resilience and the reliability of information.He said modern warfare was no longer limited to conventional fighting along national borders. It now included asymmetric warfare, proxy conflicts, cyberattacks, drone swarms, information operations and attempts to shape public narratives.Singh described Bagdogra as a strategically important location and a key part of India's security framework, particularly for the North-Eastern region.He praised the personnel stationed there for their courage and commitment, saying their presence provided a strong defence shield for India's eastern sector. He added that their preparedness was essential to maintaining stability in the region.ALSO READ | World's highest IL-76 landing, Nyoma makes mark as India's key airbase on the LACGet the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Accused who shot ex-Tech Mahindra regional head Paramjeet Dhankar dead arrested
articles.summary: FARIDABAD: A 44-year-old scrap dealer who allegedly shot dead his 42-year-old neighbour, Paramjeet Dhankar, a former regional business head of Tech
articles.body: FARIDABAD: A 44-year-old scrap dealer who allegedly shot dead his 42-year-old neighbour, Paramjeet Dhankar, a former regional business head of Tech Mahindra's Asia-Pacific region, following a parking dispute in Faridabad, has been arrested from DLF Chowk in Ballabgarh, police said on Saturday.The accused, identified as Mohan alias Monu Sharma, allegedly opened fire at Dhankar in Sector 21C on Friday night, killing him on the spot.According to police, the accused fired around 14-15 rounds, three to four of which hit Dhankar, killing him on the spot.Dhankar lived on the first floor of house number 641 with his wife, son and daughter, while the accused resided on the third floor of the same building.Police said Dhankar had returned home from the gym around 8pm when an argument broke out between the two men over vehicle parking. The altercation escalated, following which Mohan allegedly pulled out his licensed pistol and opened fire.Investigators are also probing whether an earlier dispute involving a pet dog contributed to the shooting.According to police, the two families had been involved in repeated disputes. Five days before the incident, Mohan had allegedly abused Dhankar's son. The victim's family had also approached the police with a complaint over the dispute a few days earlier, but the matter was subsequently settled.Dhankar was employed with a private company in Singapore and had returned to Faridabad just two days before the shooting to attend his nephew's wedding, scheduled for November 24. He originally hailed from Hisar.According to his LinkedIn profile, Dhankar had earlier served as regional business head of Tech Mahindra's Asia-Pacific region. He was currently working as senior vice-president of FPT Software Company Limited.Stay updated with the latest Faridabad news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Watch: PM Modi's Diwali greetings for nation; will continue tradition of meeting soldiers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended Diwali greetings to people across the country and said he would continue the tradition of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended Diwali greetings to people across the country and said he would continue the tradition of celebrating the festival with soldiers.In a video message posted on X, PM Modi said the country was being illuminated with lights on the eve of Diwali, reflecting its resolve to fight darkness."My heartiest greetings to all of you for Diwali. I wish for peace, prosperity and happiness for all of you in the coming days. I also celebrate Deepavali like you with great enthusiasm," he said."As you know, it is my annual tradition to spend the festival with the brave soldiers of our country, and I will continue that tradition this year as well," he said, adding, "Have a great Diwali".However, he did not reveal where he would celebrate the festival this year.Earlier, in a message posted on the government's Jan Sampark Portal, PM Modi said Diwali celebrates the victory of light over darkness, goodness over evil and hope over despair."Dear fellow citizen, warm greetings on the auspicious occasion of Diwali! This festival celebrates the eternal victory of light over darkness, goodness over evil and hope over despair," the Prime Minister said."May Diwali illuminate every home with happiness, harmony and prosperity. May this festive season inspire us to spread kindness, embrace positivity and work towards a brighter future," he said."Once again, wishing you a Happy Diwali," he added.Earlier in the day, PM Modi also met Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan and exchanged Diwali greetings. Sharing details of the meeting on X, the Prime Minister said, "Met Vice President Thiru CP Radhakrishnan Ji and exchanged Diwali greetings."PM Modi had earlier extended his wishes to people on Dhanteras, which marks the beginning of the five-day Diwali festivities.In a post on X, he said, "Wishing all my fellow citizens boundless happiness on Dhanteras. May the divine grace of Lord Dhanvantari forever fill everyone’s life with happiness, peace, and excellent health."The Diwali celebrations began with Dhanteras on November 6 followed by Choti Diwali on November 7. The main festival, along with Lakshmi Puja will be observed on November 8.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Grow up, Pramila’: Harmeet Dhillon hits back at Democrat leader Jayapal over ‘knitting’ jibe after DOJ exit
articles.summary: Former Department of Justice official Harmeet Dhillon responds to Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's jibe over her knitting hobby and tenure, asserting the importance of public service amid criticism of her civil rights record.
articles.body: Former US Justice Department official Harmeet Dhillon has hit back at Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal after the Democrat criticised her tenure at the department and made a sarcastic reference to her knitting hobby, telling the lawmaker to stop engaging in personal attacks and focus on her responsibilities as a public servant.Pramila accused the former official of weakening the division's civil rights mission by targeting diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programmes and pressuring states over voter registration records.“Harmeet Dhillon made a mockery of the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division by attacking diversity, equity, and inclusion and bullying states into disenfranchising voters,” Jayapal wrote on X.“She will not be missed. Enjoy your knitting,” she added.Dhillon responded by questioning Jayapal's conduct as an elected representative and describing her comments as bullying and trolling.“Grow up, Pramila. Bullying and trolling are not really the role of members of Congress. You are a public servant. Act like it,” she wrote.She also defended knitting as a useful skill rather than something to be mocked, saying it could contribute to a balanced life.“By the way, knitting is a skill. Acquiring some skills is part of a healthy, balanced life. I recommend this to you. No need to be hateful all day!” Dhillon added.The social media exchange followed Dhillon's resignation as head of the Civil Rights Division, which Attorney General Todd Blanche announced on Thursday. She had held the position since April last year.During her time in office, Dhillon shifted the division's focus towards challenging DEI policies, pursuing cases involving alleged discrimination and enforcing federal election laws. Her approach drew criticism from Democrats and civil rights advocates, who argued that the department was moving away from its traditional responsibility of protecting civil rights.One major point of disagreement was the department's attempts to obtain voter registration data from states to examine potential non-citizen voting. Dhillon's division pursued legal action against states that did not provide the requested records and sent election monitors to polling locations.Dhillon's departure also followed a significant turnover among career staff at the Civil Rights Division. More than 75% of its workforce from the beginning of President Donald Trump's second term had left by the time she resigned, according to AP.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Ayodhya glows with 30 lakh diyas as Deepotsav lights up Saryu ghats on Diwali eve
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ayodhya bathed in the glow of millions of earthen lamps on Saturday as the city celebrated the 10th edition of its grand Deepotsav festival
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ayodhya bathed in the glow of millions of earthen lamps on Saturday as the city celebrated the 10th edition of its grand Deepotsav festival along the banks of the Saryu River.Lakhs of diyas illuminated Ram Ki Paidi ghat, while more than 30 lakh earthen lamps were set to light up 56 ghats along the river, turning the temple town into a spectacular sea of lights.The annual celebration, which marks the return of Lord Ram to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana, recreates the traditional welcome believed to have been given to him by the people of the city in the Treta Yuga.The grand event was attended by Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, Uttar Pradesh governor Anandiben Patel and chief minister Yogi Adityanath, along with saints and other dignitaries.Ayodhya's spiritual and cultural showcaseEarlier in the evening, Adityanath and Patel welcomed the Vice President to Ayodhya. The dignitaries took part in prayers and rituals dedicated to Lord Ram and Goddess Janaki before the chief minister addressed a gathering at Ram Katha Park.Adityanath described the festival as a symbol of Ayodhya's transformation, recalling the long struggle surrounding the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and the sacrifices made by kar sevaks and saints.He also highlighted the city's development under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, pointing to the inauguration of the Ram temple and the expansion of infrastructure, including the international airport named after Maharishi Valmiki.The chief minister also criticised political leaders who had opposed the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, saying they should apologise to devotees and saints for their past actions.Also read: Akhilesh, Dimple Yadav to visit Ram Temple in Ayodhya on Dec 12, says SP leader Pandey ahead of UP pollsGovernor hails Ayodhya's popularity Governor Anandiben Patel said Ayodhya's growing popularity as a pilgrimage and tourist destination was creating economic opportunities for local residents.She noted that the rise in visitors had opened up avenues for employment in hospitality, transport, food services, handicrafts, flower offerings and other local businesses.Vice President Radhakrishnan was the chief guest at the celebrations. Adityanath welcomed him and praised his journey from a farming family in Tamil Nadu to one of the country's highest constitutional offices.Ahead of the main programme, the chief minister also visited an exhibition showcasing Ayodhya's 500-year history, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and the city's recent infrastructure development.Thousands of volunteers were involved in arranging the lamps along the riverfront. More than 2,500 police personnel, along with specialised security teams, were deployed to manage the crowds and ensure security during the celebrations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Video: Scuffle over doorway space inside moving Mumbai local train, one passenger tumbles onto platform
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A passenger fell onto a railway platform after a fight broke out between commuters inside a Churchgate-Virar fast local, according to an undated
articles.body: MUMBAI: A passenger fell onto a railway platform after a fight broke out between commuters inside a Churchgate-Virar fast local, according to an undated video that has surfaced on social media. The incident reportedly took place between Grant Road and Mumbai Central stations.The video shows two passengers engaged in a scuffle near the doorway of the moving train following an argument over standing near the entrance. During the altercation, one of them appears to fall out of the train onto the platform.The exact date and circumstances of the incident could not be independently established. Railway police said no complaint had been registered with the Government Railway Police (GRP) in connection with the incident. Preliminary information suggests that the passenger who fell may not have sustained serious injuries and left the station without approaching the police.A GRP officer said the railway station could not be identified from the video and that nobody had approached any GRP police station to report the incident. He added that the police were making efforts to identify the station. Further action would be taken after examining the CCTV footage.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: A Florida landowner won $40,000 after a telecom company laid fibre cables outside an easement; the state's highest court has now ruled that an old legal-fees clause does not automatically bind later property owners
articles.summary: A property agreement can continue to affect land even after the original owners have sold it.
articles.body: A property agreement can continue to affect land even after the original owners have sold it. But do all the conditions in such an agreement automatically apply to future owners? The Florida Supreme Court has addressed this question in a dispute involving a telecommunications company that installed underground fibre-optic cables beyond an authorised easement. The property owner won $40,000 in trespass damages, but a separate dispute over legal fees eventually reached the state's highest court.In an opinion dated October 29, 2026, the Florida Supreme Court ruled that an agreement requiring the losing party to pay the winner's attorney fees does not automatically apply to future property owners. The ruling came in RJ's International Trading, LLC v. Crown Castle South, LLC, case number SC2024-0547, with the opinion available on Justia. The court answered a legal question referred by the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit about when contractual obligations can pass to subsequent owners.How the dispute beganThe dispute dates back more than three decades, when Hidden Valley Corporation owned two neighbouring properties in Miami. It leased one property to BellSouth Mobility and allowed the telecommunications company to use part of the adjoining property for its operations. The arrangement was formalised through an easement agreement. An easement gives someone the legal right to use another person's property for a specific purpose without owning it. In this case, the agreement permitted the telecommunications company and its successors to use a defined portion of the neighbouring land.The agreement also stated that if either party filed a lawsuit to enforce its terms, the losing party would have to pay the successful party's reasonable attorney fees and court costs. Over the years, ownership of the properties changed hands. Eventually, RJ's International Trading LLC (RJI) acquired the property covered by the easement, while Crown Castle South LLC exercised rights under the agreement through a sublease from BellSouth.Fibre cables installed beyond the easementThe dispute arose in 2020, when Crown Castle excavated parts of RJI's property outside the authorised easement and installed underground fibre-optic cables. RJI filed a lawsuit in the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, alleging trespass and breach of the easement agreement, among other claims.The district court found that Crown Castle had gone beyond the authorised boundaries. The case then proceeded to a six-day jury trial to determine damages. The jury awarded RJI $1 for breach of the easement agreement and $40,000 for trespass. It declined to award punitive damages.After the verdict, RJI sought additional attorney fees under the original agreement. It argued that the legal-fees clause was attached to the property and should therefore apply to later owners as well. However, the district court rejected the request, finding that the clause was not sufficiently connected to the property's use or enjoyment to automatically bind future owners.Why the legal-fees clause became importantRJI challenged the decision, taking the dispute to the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals. The appeals court sought clarification from the Florida Supreme Court on whether an attorney-fees clause in an easement agreement could automatically apply to people who acquired the property later. The Eleventh Circuit had separately considered whether RJI could claim the benefit of the provision as a party to the original agreement. However, that question was not part of the legal issue referred to the Florida Supreme Court. The central question was whether a contractual promise to pay legal expenses could become a permanent obligation attached to the land, even when a future owner had not signed the original agreement.The Florida Supreme Court explained that not every condition in a property agreement automatically applies to future owners. For an obligation to continue after a property is sold, it must have a direct connection to the land and its use or enjoyment. The court found that the attorney-fees clause did not meet this requirement. It dealt with who would pay legal expenses if a dispute went to court, rather than how the property could be used or maintained.How the court distinguished an earlier rulingThe justices also compared the dispute with Hayslip v. U.S. Home Corp., a 2022 Florida Supreme Court decision involving an arbitration clause in a property deed. In that earlier case, the court allowed the arbitration provision to apply to future owners because it concerned construction defects that could affect the condition of a home.The justices said the two situations were different. While construction-related arbitration could directly affect the property, an attorney-fees clause simply determines who pays legal costs after a dispute. It does not determine how the land is used or enjoyed. The court therefore ruled that the legal-fees provision could not automatically bind subsequent property owners.What happens next?The Florida Supreme Court answered the Eleventh Circuit's question in the negative and sent the matter back to the federal appeals court for further proceedings. The decision does not cancel RJI's earlier $40,000 trespass award. Instead, it clarifies that a legal-fees clause in an old property agreement does not automatically become an obligation for everyone who owns the land later.The ruling draws a distinction between conditions that directly concern a property's use and contractual terms that deal only with expenses arising from legal disputes.You use AI every day. articles.title: UK bride’s father was hospitalised with heart failure just days before her wedding; then she brought her wedding dress to his hospital room for a father-daughter dance
articles.summary: For Sinead Jackson, having her father walk her down the aisle was one of the moments she had looked forward to most at her wedding.
articles.body: For Sinead Jackson, having her father walk her down the aisle was one of the moments she had looked forward to most at her wedding. But just days before she was due to marry her partner, Stephen, her father, Leslie Healy, was admitted to hospital with a heart problem and was told he was too unwell to attend the ceremony.Rather than let the moment pass without him, Sinead found a way to share part of her wedding day with her father. She visited him at Tameside Hospital in England, wearing her wedding dress, and the two shared a father-daughter dance on the hospital's acute cardiology unit.According to a report by PEOPLE, Sinead, 36, was due to marry Stephen on October 10 in Hyde, England. Her father had been taken to Tameside Hospital after experiencing shortness of breath and heart palpitations. The report said doctors discovered he was in heart failure, leaving him unable to attend the wedding or walk his daughter down the aisle.The hospital confirmed that Leslie had been admitted to the acute cardiology unit shortly before the wedding. It said he was still undergoing investigations to establish the cause of his admission.Sinead wanted her father to see her in her wedding dressThe news was difficult for Sinead, who had been looking forward to her father seeing her dressed as a bride. Speaking to PEOPLE, she recalled how her mother called to tell her that Leslie had undergone a scan and needed to remain in hospital.When the family realised he would not be able to attend, she struggled to accept the change in plans. “I couldn’t stop crying,” she recalled. “It hit because it’s your dream, isn’t it? Having your dad there to walk you down the aisle. That’s the thing I was looking forward to most.”She also explained that her father had been waiting to see her in her wedding dress. “I waited weeks for Dad to see me in my dress because when I bought it, he said he wanted to see me wear it on the day. That was the dream, to see his first reaction,” she said.Sinead considered postponing the wedding, but Leslie encouraged her to go ahead. She told that she has four brothers and her father knew they would be there to support her. However, she was determined to see him before the ceremony. “My day couldn’t go ahead until I’d seen my dad,” she said.Hospital staff helped arrange the father-daughter danceAccording to the hospital's October 16 statement, staff on the acute cardiology unit learnt that Leslie would miss his daughter's wedding and arranged for Sinead to visit him in her wedding gown. Leslie was also dressed for the occasion. The visit gave the father and daughter an opportunity to share their first dance before the wedding ceremony, with Sinead's mother, Mary, other family members and hospital staff present.Sinead said that the moment moved everyone around them. “All the nurses and all the patients were crying,” she said. Leslie also spoke about the experience in the hospital's statement. “It was a very emotional day for us all, happiness for my daughter Sinead, as well as sadness at not being able to attend,” he said.Although Leslie could not be physically present at the ceremony, the family found another way to include him. Sinead's five-year-old son, Maxy, walked her down the aisle in his grandfather's place, at Leslie's request.An uncle also video-called Leslie from the wedding so he could watch his daughter walk down the aisle. According to PEOPLE, he followed the ceremony virtually from his hospital room. Sinead said seeing her father before the wedding helped her feel more relaxed.Sinead and Stephen have also planned to celebrate with Leslie and take wedding photographs together once he feels better. She said she intends to wear her wedding dress again while her father puts on his suit.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Did Abdul El-Sayed get his Wikipedia page edited to soften controversial sentences before Michigan Senate election? Larry Sanger responds
articles.summary: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's Wikipedia page was allegedly edited over several months to soften or remove references to controversies
articles.body: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's Wikipedia page was allegedly edited over several months to soften or remove references to controversies surrounding him ahead of the November 3 election, according to an investigation by researchers who tracked changes to the online encyclopedia.The edits were reportedly made by an anonymous Wikipedia contributor using the username "CopyleftEverything", who changed descriptions of El-Sayed's medical credentials, his association with left-wing influencer Hasan Piker and controversies involving Michigan's Jewish community.Investigative journalist Ashley Rindsberg, founder of the online campaign-influence tracker NPOV, and New York-based researcher Yehuda Teitelbaum separately examined the page's revision history and highlighted the changes on X.Rindsberg said the editor had been carrying out what appeared to be a systematic clean-up of El-Sayed's Wikipedia profile in the run-up to the election.One of the changes was made on June 12, when the wording describing El-Sayed's medical qualifications was altered. The original statement that he "has never been granted a medical license" was replaced with the softer phrase "did not pursue a medical license".El-Sayed holds a Doctor of Medicine degree from Columbia University but did not complete residency training or obtain a medical licence. During the election campaign, he faced criticism for referring to himself as a doctor.Another change involved Hasan Piker, the left-wing Twitch streamer and political commentator who appeared alongside El-Sayed at two Democratic primary-night events in April.On October 10, the description of Piker was changed from "a controversial left-wing Twitch streamer and political commentator" to "left-wing political commentator", removing the word "controversial".Piker has previously faced criticism for saying that America "deserved" the September 11, 2001, terror attacks.The researchers also flagged changes involving El-Sayed's relationship with Michigan's Jewish community. Two paragraphs, removed on October 12 and October 31, had referred to his appointment of a Jewish community liaison officer amid tensions over his criticism of the Israeli government, opposition to US military aid to Israel and remarks following the March 12 attack on Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield.El-Sayed had faced criticism for saying "hurt people hurt people" while discussing the synagogue attacker's relatives, who were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon. He later apologized for the remark.The Wikipedia edits also drew a response from the platform's co-founder Larry Sanger, who described Rindsberg's findings as "old-fashioned journalism". He said the reporting was "both appropriate and effective as a criticism of Wikipedia and how it works today".Wikipedia operates on an open-editing model that allows users, including anonymous contributors, to modify articles. Changes can be made directly, although contributors are generally expected to support information with verifiable sources.Teitelbaum questioned the implications of the edits, arguing that Wikipedia's influence extends beyond the platform because Google search results and artificial intelligence systems frequently rely on its content."This is just not a random event to correct the public record," he told the New York Post. "This was really an organized effort to change the narrative in this country and to portray narratives and certain ideas that are not honest."El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the November 3 Michigan Senate election. His victory makes him the first Muslim American elected to the US SenateYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pisces, Weekly Horoscope, November 08 to November 14, 2026: Important decisions and relationship matters shape the week
articles.summary: This week begins with a slight drag in the heart, Pisces. Monday may feel heavier than it really is, as though your mood wakes up before your hope does.
articles.body: This week begins with a slight drag in the heart, Pisces. Monday may feel heavier than it really is, as though your mood wakes up before your hope does. Work may present a few snags, and even small delays can irritate you more than usual. Drive carefully, keep your words measured, and don’t pick a fight just because your patience is thin. A little discomfort in the body, especially around the leg, can also lower your spirits. Some days are like damp mornings. You still get on with things, but the sun takes its time.The good news is that the sky clears quickly. Tuesday changes the rhythm in your favour and brings a stronger sense of success. Children do well, students feel focused, and the home atmosphere becomes easier to enjoy. Confidence returns. By Wednesday, luck seems to step in with a helping hand, especially around money and family pride. Good news from children, perhaps linked to studies, awards, or recognition, lifts your social image too. Still, your thoughts may remain somewhat unsettled even while events improve. That’s classic Pisces this week, blessings in hand, doubts still circling like late birds.Thursday and Friday deepen the positive turn. Spiritual interest rises, family support grows, and work stress reduces. Friday in particular helps smooth practical matters, while also bringing relief connected to your father’s health. Keep a careful eye on your mother’s condition though, especially if she has been neglecting rest or routine treatment. By Saturday, respect and recognition bloom in a bigger way. Society, colleagues, or relatives may speak well of you. Orders, opportunities, and praise can come together. Yet even on your best day, confusion nips at the edge. So smile, accept the good, but think twice before major commitments.Love and Relationships:Love starts the week on uneven ground, Pisces. Monday can bring friction with your spouse, and romance may feel dry or disappointing. If you’re already carrying unspoken irritation, a careless sentence could turn into a full argument. Speak softly. This is not the day to prove a point. If you are dating someone, lower expectations for dramatic closeness at the start of the week. Give each other breathing space. Sometimes affection returns faster when nobody chases it.Tuesday brings much better emotional weather. Harmony with your spouse improves, and lovers may finally get time together without interruptions or mixed signals. You’ll notice that your mood softens when everyday pressure drops. That pattern continues, though Wednesday asks for care again. There may be tension with your spouse that could leave a lasting bitter taste if handled badly. Don’t drag old history into a new disagreement. Listen first. If the issue is about family, money, or time management, solve the actual matter instead of attacking the person.From Thursday onward, the heart opens beautifully. Romance grows stronger, and your affection toward your spouse becomes more visible, more generous, more sincere. Friday adds a particularly warm touch, even in a busy schedule. You may still be occupied with work, but quality time becomes possible if you make space for it. A shared meal, a walk after dinner, or a quiet cup of tea can do wonders. Saturday keeps love in a positive zone, though your own uncertainty may make you overthink a good moment. Don’t spoil sweetness by searching for hidden problems. Let closeness be simple this weekend.Education and Career:The week opens with some friction at work. Monday may test your patience through delays, mismatched expectations, or a task that takes longer than planned. Nothing here says failure, only that you must stay steady and not react sharply. Speak carefully with colleagues, clients, and seniors. If you’re commuting for work, leave a little earlier and avoid careless driving. Students may not find Monday especially inspiring either, so use it for revision rather than trying to conquer everything at once.Tuesday brings a much stronger current for effort and achievement. Students can focus well, confidence rises, and the mind settles enough to absorb information properly. If exams, presentations, or submissions are close, this is a fine day to build momentum. Wednesday continues the positive trend in a broader way. Luck supports you, and children or younger people in the family may earn appreciation that reflects well on the household. If you work in education, management, sales, or public-facing roles, your standing improves through visible results rather than loud self-promotion.Thursday is good for business owners who want to start something new. The day carries courage and backing from family, which matters more than people admit. By Friday, your work atmosphere becomes noticeably smoother. Worries reduce. You may connect with influential people who can help your career, whether through advice, references, introductions, or future openings. Students also regain strong focus here. There may be discussion of property through your spouse’s name or family link, which could later affect your practical planning. Saturday is the brightest career day of the week. Orders may come from several sides for business people, and public respect grows. Just don’t make hurried decisions because success arrives all at once.Money and Finance:Your money story begins cautiously but improves fast, Pisces. Monday can tempt you toward speculation, and the indications are not bad, but your mood is. That matters. Don’t place money decisions in the hands of a restless mind. If you invest, do it after checking details, not while upset after an argument or rough commute. Keep spending plain and practical at the start of the week.Tuesday and Wednesday bring stronger financial luck. Speculation can work in your favour, and gains may come beyond expectation by midweek. This could be profit, a payment, a refund, a bonus, or simply money arriving from a source you had not counted on. Good news from children may also reduce future expense pressure or increase your pride in where your resources are going. There is a feeling of fortune opening a side window for you. Don’t waste that by becoming careless.Thursday is good for business people launching a fresh venture, and Friday may bring property-related benefit through your spouse’s side or name. That sounds promising, but read every paper calmly and don’t let family excitement run ahead of facts. Saturday is excellent for social standing and business orders, and once again favourable for speculation. Yet this day also carries low self-reliance and mild confusion. Strange combination, no? Money can come, praise can come, and still your judgement may wobble. So make a simple rule. No big financial move without one night of sleep and one sensible second opinion. That will save you from avoidable mistakes.Health and Well-being:Take care of your body at the start of the week, Pisces. Monday may bring slight sadness, and that emotional dip can show itself physically through tiredness, irritation, or pain in the left leg. Don’t ignore small discomfort just because the day is busy. Also, drive carefully. Your chart this week suggests that carelessness, rushing, and distraction are bigger risks than actual illness. Slow down a little. Even your speech needs handling with care, because stress can make you sharper than you intend.Tuesday brings a welcome lift. Health stays sound, your mood improves, and the body feels more cooperative. Use that better energy wisely. Catch up on sleep, eat properly, and return to a routine that supports you instead of draining you. Wednesday keeps health normal, though the mind may continue to flutter with too many thoughts. If you can, reduce noise in the evening. Less screen time, fewer unnecessary calls, and one peaceful meal can help settle your nervous system.Thursday and Friday are supportive for overall balance. Spiritual activity can be soothing, almost like cool shade in a hot afternoon. Family happiness also improves your emotional state. You may feel better simply because the people around you are easier to deal with. Friday asks you to be mindful about your mother’s health and somewhat relieved regarding your father’s improvement. Saturday is strong and uplifting, but mentally mixed. Respect and success energise you, yet confusion can still tire you if you keep replaying decisions. Trust your body’s signals. Rest when needed. Clear your head before sleep. A calm mind will protect your health better than any tonic this week.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: 'AQI likely to worsen tomorrow': Delhi chokes under thick smog on Diwali eve; readings in several areas cross 400
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi's air quality remained in the 'very poor' category on Saturday, with an AQI of 369 as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city on the eve
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi's air quality remained in the 'very poor' category on Saturday, with an AQI of 369 as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city on the eve of Diwali, reducing visibility.The situation is likely to worsen on Sunday, with air quality expected to remain in the 'severe' category on Diwali, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS).The outlook for the subsequent six days indicates that air quality is likely to fluctuate between the 'severe' and 'very poor' categories.Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data, 16 reported 'severe' air quality, while 29 recorded levels in the 'very poor' category. The highest AQI of 452 was recorded near IIT Delhi.The city's average AQI improved slightly from 382 on Friday to 369 on Saturday, remaining close to the 'severe' threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating a deterioration in air quality across the capital city.As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, the onset of Diwali-related celebrations and vehicular emissions, and the peak period of stubble burning in neighbouring states.Unfavourable weather conditions are further worsening the pollution situation. According to the EWS, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, along with an average wind speed of less than 10 kilometres per hour, hampers the effective dispersion of pollutants.PM10 was the predominant pollutant in the national capital on Saturday.According to the Decision Support System (DSS) for Delhi, the transport sector was the largest contributor to the city's pollution on Saturday, accounting for 21.4 per cent. The contribution of stubble burning was pegged at 1.7 per cent, with forecasts suggesting that it might go up to 5.4 per cent on Sunday.Satellite data detected 589 farm fire incidents across six states on Friday. Punjab accounted for the highest number at 357, followed by Madhya Pradesh (139), Rajasthan (58), Uttar Pradesh (23), Haryana (nine) and Uttarakhand (three).Between September 15 and November 6, a total of 6,226 stubble-burning incidents were recorded across the six states.The data was provided by the Consortium for Research on Agroecosystem Monitoring and Modelling from Space (CREAMS) Laboratory of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute in its bulletin.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: PCOS and fertility: 5 everyday lifestyle changes that may help improve ovulation and support your chances of conceiving
articles.summary: For many women, a PCOS diagnosis brings an immediate worry: Will it affect the chances of becoming a mother?
articles.body: For many women, a PCOS diagnosis brings an immediate worry: Will it affect the chances of becoming a mother? Irregular periods, hormonal changes and unpredictable ovulation can make the journey towards pregnancy confusing. But PCOS does not automatically mean infertility. Many women with the condition conceive naturally.The key lies in understanding that PCOS is not just about the ovaries. It is also linked to insulin resistance, metabolism and hormonal health. According to Dr Narendra K Shetty, Chief Wellness Officer, Kshemavana Naturopathy and Yoga Center, a combination of sensible nutrition, physical activity, adequate sleep and timely medical care can support reproductive health.Start with what goes on the plateFood choices can influence insulin levels, which matter because insulin resistance can contribute to higher androgen levels and interfere with normal ovulation.Dr Shetty recommends a balanced, largely plant-based diet containing whole grains, millets, pulses, seasonal vegetables, fruits, nuts and seeds."Particular attention should be given to including plant-based protein and fibre, choosing minimally processed grains, adding healthy fats from nuts and seeds, and cutting back on sugars, sweet drinks and highly processed foods," he explained.Instead of following restrictive diets, women can focus on sustainable eating habits that support blood sugar regulation and overall metabolic health.Move beyond exercise for weight lossPhysical activity is not simply about reducing numbers on the weighing scale. Regular movement can improve insulin sensitivity, cardiovascular health and metabolic function."Adding yoga to walking, cycling and resistance work can give extra metabolic benefits," Dr Shetty said.Practices such as Surya Namaskar, Trikonasana and Baddha Konasana can complement regular exercise, depending on individual ability. Adults can aim for 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity each week.However, yoga should not be treated as a cure for PCOS or a guaranteed way to restore ovulation.Do not make weight the only measure of healthPCOS affects women across different body sizes. A woman with a healthy BMI can also experience insulin resistance, irregular periods and hormonal disturbances.For women carrying excess weight, gradual and sustainable weight loss may improve insulin sensitivity and menstrual regularity. But weight alone does not tell the complete story.Fitness, blood sugar control, body composition and nutritional health deserve equal attention.Give sleep and emotional health their dueFertility conversations often focus on hormones and reproductive organs, leaving emotional well-being in the background.Yet stress, poor sleep and persistent anxiety can affect overall metabolic health. Dr Shetty recommends maintaining regular sleep timings, getting seven to nine hours of rest, practising mindfulness and incorporating breathing exercises such as Nadi Shodhana and Bhramari.These practices can support well-being, although they cannot replace medical treatment.Combine lifestyle changes with timely medical carePerhaps the most important point is that natural approaches should complement, not replace, evidence-based treatment.Women experiencing prolonged gaps between periods, irregular ovulation or difficulty conceiving should seek medical evaluation. For women with anovulatory infertility due to PCOS, letrozole is a recommended first-line ovulation-induction treatment when appropriate."An integrative approach that mixes proven care with naturopathic and yogic lifestyle changes can help support overall health and reproductive well-being," Dr Shetty explained.Herbal preparations and supplements should also be discussed with a doctor, particularly when planning pregnancy.PCOS is not a verdict on motherhood. Supporting ovulation requires attention to more than menstrual cycles. Consistent lifestyle habits, metabolic health and timely medical support can help women make informed decisions about their fertility.Disclaimer: This article is for general informational purposes and is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Women with PCOS should consult a qualified healthcare professional before making dietary, exercise or treatment changes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
